content.title: 2026 World Baseball Classic: Preview, full schedule and how to watch live
content.text: Check out our one-stop guide for baseball's world championship being staged in Tokyo, San Juan, Houston and Miami from 5-17 March.Picture by The Yomiuri ShimbunThe World Baseball Classic is back for a sixth helping, and it's shaping up to be the most exciting yet. The 2026 edition will get underway on Thursday (5 March) at the Tokyo Dome when Chinese Taipei take on Australia in the matinee. The tournament will conclude on 17 March with the final set to be held in Miami. Houston (Texas) and San Juan (Puerto Rico) will also each host one of the four pools. The WBC is also an Olympic qualifier for LA28. The two highest-placed teams from the Americas will secure a quota at the next Games. The tournament has produced three champions in holders and three-time winners Japan, the Dominican Republic and the United States. Led by the world’s best player in Shohei Ohtani and reigning World Series MVP Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Samurai Japan look poised to make another run at the championship. Four-time league MVP Ohtani will not be pitching this time, but their squad depth and team chemistry will make for a difficult team to beat. The U.S., who narrowly lost to Japan in the final three years ago, have assembled what is widely being regarded as their strongest team ever to try to reclaim the throne. League MVP Aaron Judge will anchor the line-up while the two Cy Young Award winners, Paul Skenes and Tarik Skubal, will rule the hill. It’s now or never for the USA. The Dominican Republic are just as stacked as the aforementioned two with Vladimir Guerrero Jr, Juan Soto, Julio Rodriguez and Fernando Tatis Jr as the headline acts. Albert Pujols will skipper the team, attempting to lift the trophy for the first time since 2013. Venezuela are also knocking on the door of what would be their first title, behind the likes of former National League MVP Ronald Acuna Jr, William Contreras and Ranger Suarez. In the United States, Fox Sports will air all 47 games. In Japan, Netflix; Sportsnet (English) and TVA Sports (French) in Canada; ESPN in Oceania, Pan Latin America/Caribbean and the Netherlands to name a few.
